def prime_length(string):
    
    l = len(string)
    if l == 0 or l == 1:
        return False
    for i in range(2, l):
        if l % i == 0:
            return False
    return True

# Unit test for function prime_length
def test_prime_length():
    # Test with empty string (length 0 -> not prime)
    assert prime_length("") == False

    # Test with single character (length 1 -> not prime)
    assert prime_length("a") == False

    # Test with length 2 (prime)
    assert prime_length("ab") == True

    # Test with length 3 (prime)
    assert prime_length("abc") == True

    # Test with length 4 (not prime)
    assert prime_length("abcd") == False

    # Test with length 5 (prime)
    assert prime_length("abcde") == True

    # Test with length 6 (not prime)
    assert prime_length("abcdef") == False

    # Test with length 7 (prime)
    assert prime_length("abcdefg") == True

    # Test with length 9 (not prime, 9 = 3*3)
    assert prime_length("a" * 9) == False

    # Test with length 11 (prime)
    assert prime_length("a" * 11) == True

    # Test with length 13 (prime)
    assert prime_length("hello world!!") == True

    # Test with length 16 (not prime)
    assert prime_length("a" * 16) == False

    assert prime_length("Hello, World!") == True  # length 13

    # Test with whitespace-only string of prime length
    assert prime_length("     ") == True  # length 5

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_prime_length()
